speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your gums or other mucous membranes, and a rash of tiny red spots called petechiae. To understand what is causing this, have you noticed if the bleeding stops easily when you apply pressure, or does it take a very long time?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the symptoms. Given the combination of easy mucous membrane bleeding and petechiae on the extremities, this suggests a platelet disorder. Has the child had any recent illnesses, high fevers, or been exposed to anyone with a similar viral infection?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP). The presentation of frequent epistaxis, mucous membrane bleeding, and diffuse petechiae in a previously healthy child is the classic clinical triad for acute ITP. I will order a Complete Blood Count to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_Diff.
